# What macOS and Windows CI test beyond what scripts/os-tests.sh finds by
# itself (packages built from other files there than on Linux, and test
# files with a build constraint). Linux CI runs every test; the full macOS
# suite runs nightly (.github/workflows/macos-full.yml).
#
#   GOOS PACKAGE            all of its tests
#   GOOS PACKAGE REGEX      its tagged test files' tests and those REGEX
#                           matches, instead of all of them (no spaces or
#                           slashes in REGEX)
#   GOOS PACKAGE -          none: its tests do not pass there yet
#
# Add a package whose code takes another way on that system through
# runtime.GOOS, or that drives a program only that system has.

# macOS: the host CLI, the native node agent and the sandbox.
darwin internal/hostsecrets   # the Keychain, through security(1)
darwin internal/secretxfer    # moving host secrets between machines
darwin internal/nodeagent     # launchd, exec and PATH lookup of the node agent
darwin internal/cli           # fridolin core / node / service on the host
darwin internal/sandbox       # the sandbox-exec profiles
darwin internal/site          # the site process under sandbox-exec
darwin internal/fsx           # case-insensitive and symlinked paths
darwin internal/version
# The bridge's runtime is too big to run whole on every pull request: its
# darwin files' tests, and those that branch on runtime.GOOS or pin what
# macOS writes (sandbox profiles, the starter config, the golden files).
darwin internal/app ^Test(Sandbox|SiteAPISecrets|ExampleConfigIsValid|GoldenStarterConfig|CheckRunsABrainWhoseFolderHoldsAPATHFolder|RuntimePathConsumersKeepBootAndApplyLiveOptions|CheckRedact|CheckLeavesTheMediaFolderAlone|Viewer|BridgeTellsTheSandboxItsConfigFile|BrowserProfilesDenyEveryChannel|Lock|Golden)

# Windows: the bridge runs there only in the Linux container
# (docs/CORE.md), so the native binary is the node agent and the host CLI
# and the libraries under them (docs/DECISIONS.md). These packages pass on
# Windows; one joins the list once its tests do.
windows internal/app ^$       # only its tests for Windows (^$ adds none)
windows internal/access
windows internal/activity
windows internal/apperr
windows internal/archtest
windows internal/chat
windows internal/devchat
windows internal/google
windows internal/history
windows internal/hostsecrets
windows internal/jsonx
windows internal/logx
windows internal/nodeagent
windows internal/nodeproto
windows internal/nodes
windows internal/otp
windows internal/outbound
windows internal/pipeline
windows internal/platform
windows internal/prompt
windows internal/route
windows internal/secretxfer
windows internal/store
windows internal/testutil
windows internal/textx
windows internal/toolcli
windows internal/trigger
windows internal/version
